EvidenceStatement: Roman dodecahedra are hollow cast copper-alloy objects.
Complete specimens have 12 pentagonal faces.
Each face contains one circular opening.
Hole diameters usually vary within a specimen.
Twenty knobs occur at the vertices.
Typical size is approximately 4–11 cm.
Specimens differ in overall dimensions.
Objects were produced by casting.
High manufacturing skill was required.
Surface finishing is commonly present.
Concentric rings commonly surround holes.
Decoration varies between specimens.
No authenticated inscriptions or numerals are known.
No ancient text securely explains the function.
No undisputed ancient depiction of use is known.
Finds cluster in north-western Roman provinces.
No confirmed finds are known from Italy.
Most finds date to the 2nd–4th centuries AD.
Artifacts occur in military contexts.
Artifacts occur in civilian settlements.
Artifacts occur in funerary contexts.
Artifacts occur in hoards and river deposits.
No single archaeological context dominates.
About 130 known specimens exist.
Roman Britain accounts for roughly one quarter of known finds.
Published wear evidence is limited and inconsistent.
No universal pattern of rope wear has been demonstrated.
No widespread evidence of soot or wax residues has been published.
No accepted metrological standard has been demonstrated.
More than fifty functional hypotheses have been proposed.
